settlement_wire.title: International wire
settlement_wire.what: A bank transfer across borders through a chain of banks. Each one checks it, so it takes days.
settlement_wire.why: Cheap and trusted, but slow: the supplier waits for the money, so your stock arrives later. Order earlier when you pay this way.

letter_of_credit.title: Letter of credit
letter_of_credit.what: Your bank promises the supplier it will pay as soon as the shipping papers are in order.
letter_of_credit.why: The supplier ships sooner because a bank stands behind you. It costs a fee, but protects both sides.

digital_dollars.title: Digital dollars
digital_dollars.what: Tokens that track the dollar and move between exchange accounts in minutes, any day of the week.
digital_dollars.why: Fast payment means stock moves sooner. You need an exchange account, and a new payment rail brings its own risks.

escrow.title: Escrow (pay on delivery)
escrow.what: Your money is locked with a neutral party and released to the supplier only when the goods arrive.
escrow.why: You never pay for goods that don't show up, and the supplier knows the money is there. Useful with a supplier you haven't worked with before.

net_terms.title: Payment terms (Net 30 / Net 60)
net_terms.what: The buyer pays the invoice 30 or 60 days after delivery, not on the day they get the goods.
net_terms.why: A big sale can still leave you short of cash for two months. Check the cash forecast before you say yes.

early_payment.title: Early payment discount
early_payment.what: You give up a few percent of an invoice to be paid now instead of in 60 days.
early_payment.why: It costs a little profit, but can cover payroll or rent when cash is tight.

moq.title: Minimum order (MOQ)
moq.what: The smallest quantity a supplier will sell you in one order.
moq.why: A low minimum lets you test a product cheaply; big orders tie up more cash in stock.

lead_time.title: Lead time
lead_time.what: The days between paying a supplier and the stock reaching your shelf.
lead_time.why: The longer it is, the earlier you must reorder, or you run out and lose sales.

gross_margin.title: Gross margin
gross_margin.what: What's left of a sale after the cost of the goods: price minus unit cost, as a share of the price.
gross_margin.why: Margin pays for rent, wages and ads. A busy shop with a thin margin can still lose money.

cash_vs_profit.title: Cash is not profit
cash_vs_profit.what: Profit is what you earned on paper; cash is what's in the bank today. Unpaid invoices and stock count as profit or assets, not cash.
cash_vs_profit.why: Bills are paid in cash. Plenty of profitable companies still run out of it.

foot_traffic.title: Foot traffic and conversion
foot_traffic.what: Foot traffic is how many people walk past; conversion is the share of them who come in and buy.
foot_traffic.why: Price and your rating move conversion; flyers bring more people past the door.

food_waste.title: Waste
food_waste.what: Fresh food you bought but couldn't sell before it spoiled.
food_waste.why: Every binned pastry is money spent for nothing. Order for the day you expect, not the day you hope for.

cafe_rating.title: Rating
cafe_rating.what: The stars customers give your café. They drift toward how each day felt: queues, running out, prices and service.
cafe_rating.why: A higher rating brings more customers every day, for free.

packaging_levy.title: Packaging levy
packaging_levy.what: A charge per parcel padded with plastic, under the Clean Packaging Act (Year 4).
packaging_levy.why: Recycled padding costs a little more but skips the levy, and eco-minded shoppers prefer it.

shipping_index.title: Shipping index
shipping_index.what: How expensive moving goods is compared with a normal year (1.00).
shipping_index.why: When it's high, couriers and imports cost more: raise prices, or buy closer to home.

deposit.title: Deposit
deposit.what: Money the landlord holds against damage or unpaid rent. You get it back when you leave.
deposit.why: It's still cash you can't use while the lease runs.

fitout.title: Fit-out
fitout.what: Turning an empty unit into a working shop: equipment, counter and furniture.
fitout.why: A one-off cost you earn back slowly from sales. Count it before you sign.

payroll.title: Payroll
payroll.what: Paying your staff their wages, every Friday at 17:00 from the company account.
payroll.why: Missing payroll hurts morale fast. Keep at least a week of wages in the bank.

stock_location.title: A second stock location
stock_location.what: Somewhere else you can keep stock, with its own space limit. An order is packed from the place that has the goods.
stock_location.why: Warehouse space costs far less per unit than an office, and more room means bigger orders and fewer sell-outs. But each location's rent is due every month, full or empty.

own_van_shipping.title: Own van or courier?
own_van_shipping.what: Delivering parcels yourself in your own van: you pay fuel per parcel instead of the courier's price, and they arrive the same day.
own_van_shipping.why: It is much cheaper per parcel, but the driving is your time. For a small batch, or when you are busy, a courier can still be the better deal.

fuel_cost.title: Fuel and running costs
fuel_cost.what: The litres you burn follow the kilometres you drive, and wear and tear add a little more on every kilometre.
fuel_cost.why: Every kilometre you don't need to drive comes straight off your costs. A shorter route saves fuel and hours.

vehicle_insurance.title: Vehicle insurance
vehicle_insurance.what: A monthly premium that covers accidents, theft and damage to your van and what is in it.
vehicle_insurance.why: It is due every month whether the van moves or not, so a van that sits idle still costs you money.

delivery_run.title: Delivery runs: pay and deadlines
delivery_run.what: A client posts a job with several stops, a fee and a deadline. On time pays the full fee, late pays less, and a run left undone is cancelled.
delivery_run.why: What you earn is the fee minus fuel, upkeep and your time. Take the runs you can finish before the deadline.

route_planning.title: Route planning
route_planning.what: The order you visit the stops in. The shortest round trip is rarely the order on the client's list.
route_planning.why: A shorter route burns less fuel and takes less time, so the run finishes earlier and pays a little more.

driver_staff.title: Van driver
driver_staff.what: An employee who takes your van out on one posted run each workday and banks the fee. They plan the route less well than you do.
driver_staff.why: It frees your hours for other work, but the weekly wage is due whether or not a run pays. Margins are thin, so it only pays with enough runs on the board.

van_capacity.title: Van capacity
van_capacity.what: How many parcels fit in one trip. The rest wait for the next trip.
van_capacity.why: A fuller van spreads the fixed time of a trip over more parcels, so each parcel costs less to deliver.

rail_reliability.title: Rail reliability
rail_reliability.what: The share of payments on a payment route that landed on time. It moves when something goes wrong on the route, and recovers slowly as payments land.
rail_reliability.why: A fast route that fails one time in ten can cost more than a slow one that never does. Look at the record, not just the speed.

frozen_funds.title: Frozen funds
frozen_funds.what: Money you have paid that is stuck on the way: the operator paused transfers, so it has not reached the supplier and has not come back to you.
frozen_funds.why: It is still yours on paper, but you cannot spend it. Keep enough cash outside any single payment route to run the business while it is stuck.

bridge_loan.title: Bridge loan
bridge_loan.what: A short loan that covers a gap until money you are owed comes in.
bridge_loan.why: The interest costs far less than missing payroll or rent. Repay it as soon as the money arrives.

kyc.title: KYC check (know your customer)
kyc.what: Before a large payment moves, the bank confirms who is paying and who is being paid.
kyc.why: It costs a fee and about a day. Order early, so the delay does not leave your shelves empty.

import_licence.title: Import licence
import_licence.what: A yearly permit from City Hall to bring goods in from abroad for business.
import_licence.why: Without a valid one, imports are blocked. Renew it before it lapses, or your next order cannot go out.

compliance_cost.title: Compliance cost
compliance_cost.what: The steady cost of following the rules: filings, checks and the person who keeps them in order.
compliance_cost.why: It is an operating cost, like rent. Build it into your prices, especially as you grow.

valuation.title: Valuation (what a buyer pays)
valuation.what: A buyer usually pays a multiple of yearly profit, plus the company's cash and stock, minus what it owes.
valuation.why: It shows what your business is worth today, and why both profit and cash matter.

earn_out.title: Earn-out
earn_out.what: Part of the price is paid later, and only if the company keeps hitting agreed targets.
earn_out.why: You can ask for a higher headline price, but you carry the risk after the sale.

purchase_cancel.title: Purchase cancellation
purchase_cancel.what: Cancel a purchase still on the way within the supplier cancellation window (normally 24 hours). The normal fee is 5%; payments that have not cleared return the full principal.
purchase_cancel.why: Fix a wrong order before it arrives. Settlement fees stay paid; an unpaid invoice is reduced instead of returning cash.

purchase_return.title: Supplier returns
purchase_return.what: Local suppliers normally accept stock within 14 days of arrival. You can return only unsold, unreserved units at the original delivery location.
purchase_return.why: Stock leaves now. Pay freight now; the supplier refunds the original purchase price less the restocking fee after receiving it, normally in 3 days.

restocking_fee.title: Restocking fee
restocking_fee.what: The supplier normally deducts 15% of the original purchase value on a return. Aurelia Makers charges no cancellation or restocking fee.
restocking_fee.why: Refunds use the original purchase price. Your books remove stock at its current average cost; the difference is an expense or other income.

contract_closure.title: Contracts after company closure
contract_closure.what: Unanswered offers are withdrawn; undelivered contracts are terminated without an extra penalty. Unpaid delivered invoices are sold to a collector in the liquidation.
contract_closure.why: The existing liquidation pays 80% of receivables once. The closed company cannot collect again or use your new company stock; old contracts remain visible as records.

loan_eligibility.title: Loan eligibility
loan_eligibility.what: Check all six lending conditions before signing. A missed condition shows its gap and where to fix it.
loan_eligibility.why: An appointment gets you to Marcus; it does not waive the company, account, credit, payment history, age or collateral requirements.

side_stories.title: Side stories
side_stories.what: Short business stories you can accept from Opportunities on your phone.
side_stories.why: Your company and its progress unlock opportunities. Complete the steps to earn contacts; unavailable opportunities end without a reward.
